The workflow error vocabulary is NOT in `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py`, and there is **no `_workflow_caller_code` and no `invalid_input` code anywhere in the tree** (grep-confirmed). The real home is the top-level **`src/rebar/_errors.py`**: `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (15 codes) + `error_code_for()` (7 precedence branches). `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py` holds only reconciler *exception* classes (JiraAPIError, RetryExhaustedError, …), not error codes. 35ab's "→ invalid_input" is not present in the current tree.

### Surface 1 — `error_code_for` + `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (`src/rebar/_errors.py`)
15 codes: ticket_not_found, store_uninitialized, show_failed, deps_failed, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, invalid_ticket_type, tracker_root_unresolved, criterion_unknown_id, criterion_registry_malformed, criterion_missing_file, llm_unavailable, config_unreadable, config_insecure_url, command_failed.

2. TicketNotFoundError → ticket_not_found — **accurate**

### Surface 4 — MCP envelope guard (`_mcp_errors.py::_envelope_error`)

8 classes (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION). comments.body:
## PREVENTION RECOMMENDATION (systemic guardrail against regressing the whole class)

The root cause is a **blanket base-class arm** (`isinstance(exc, LLMError) -> "llm_unavailable"`) that silently absorbs every NEW subclass added under `LLMError` (and, symmetrically, any new `err.error_code` string that drifts from `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`). A new subclass ships misclassified with zero signal. Recommend TWO complementary guardrails, both **portable (in-process pytest, no CI-provider dependency)** so they satisfy `project.portability`:

**1. Exhaustive exception→code contract test (the load-bearing one).**
A `tests/unit/test_error_code_contract.py` that, via `LLMError.__subclasses__()` (recursed) — i.e. the FULL live subclass set — asserts every concrete `LLMError` subclass maps under `error_code_for()` to an **explicitly enumerated** intended code, from a table checked into the test. A subclass NOT in the table fails the test with "new LLMError subclass X has no declared error code — add it to the contract (do not let it ride the `llm_unavailable` fallthrough)." This converts "silently rides the catch-all" into a hard, local failure at the moment the subclass is introduced. Extend the same pattern to `_structured_llm_failure` (Surface 2) and the `coverage.llm_unavailable` producers (Surface 3) so all three sites are pinned to the same table — that is what makes it a CLASS fix, not a per-instance one.

**2. Vocabulary-closure test.**
Assert (a) every string literal assigned to `.error_code` in `src/rebar` (AST-scan or a small registry) is a member of `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` — this catches the `pinned_ticket_read_failed` gap (0aee) and any future drift; and (b) every code in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` is reachable/produced somewhere (no dead vocabulary).

**Why a test over a lint/plan-review criterion:** the mapping is data-driven and lives in one module, so a unit test that reflects over the live subclass tree is both cheaper and MORE complete than a reviewer heuristic — it cannot be forgotten and needs no LLM. A plan-review/code-review criterion ("new exception subclass must declare an error code, never widen a catch-all") is a useful ADVISORY backstop for the design intent, but the contract test is the enforcement.

**Net effect:** adding `class NewThing(LLMError)` without a deliberate code decision breaks the build locally, so no future subclass can silently inherit the "the AI provider is down" misclassification — the exact regression path that produced 35ab/551b/73d8 and the three sites found in this audit.

## RE-TRIAGE against the refined bar (accurate-fit-to-scenario-set, not narrowness)

Applied the sharpened standard to every mapping. Net effect: **most findings collapse to `ready-to-fix` with one existing broad-accurate code (`command_failed`)** — no new vocabulary — and several previously-noted "lossy" items are re-confirmed as ACCEPTABLE (accurate-but-broad), not findings.

### The single unifying correction (covers 5f96, 7d47, fbc0, and 73d8/551b)
Narrow every `llm_unavailable` producer so it fires **only for `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError`** — whose scenario set (extra absent, credentials missing/invalid, provider unreachable/rate-limited/refused) accurately fits the name. Every other `LLMError` subclass → **`command_failed`** (existing, broad, honest: "an unclassified rebar command failure"), which makes no false cause claim for input rejections, tool-loop/budget self-stops, context-window, output defects, or workflow/expression faults. This is discriminating by exception TYPE, not by phase — which is why it also dissolves the dbca-AC3 execute-time tension in 73d8 (a real execute-time outage is an `LLMUnavailableError` and stays `llm_unavailable`).

### Re-tags applied
- **7d47** (render_workflow) escalate → **ready-to-fix** (target `command_failed`).
- **fbc0** (_structured_llm_failure) escalate → **ready-to-fix** (narrow to `LLMUnavailableError`, else `command_failed`).
- **5f96** stays **ready-to-fix** (the root branch-6 change; recommendation sharpened to `command_failed`, explicitly NOT split into narrow codes).
- **0aee** stays **ready-to-fix** — reclassified: NOT a misleading/ambiguous mapping, it is a vocabulary-registration gap (emitted code ∉ KNOWN_ERROR_CODES). Fix = add it to the frozenset.
- **f75f** stays **escalate** — a genuine AMBIGUOUS finding (`coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean implies provider-down but its scenario set includes input-rejection). No existing broad-accurate CODE swap fixes a named boolean consumed by 3 readers → contract decision.

### Re-confirmed ACCEPTABLE (accurate-but-broad — NOT findings under the refined bar)
- **branch 7 `command_failed` fallback** — honestly "an unclassified failure"; that is exactly what the branch catches. Accurate-but-broad.
- **`NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` fallback (failure.py)** — honestly "unclassified — inspect the diagnostic." Accurate-but-broad.
- **missing-[agents]-extra → NEEDS_INVESTIGATION** — the classifier cannot import the typed arms without the extra, so "unclassified" is an honest read; deliberate totality guarantee. Not a finding.
- **deps `"not found" in message ? ticket_not_found : deps_failed`** — even on a sniff misfire it lands on `deps_failed` ("the deps command failed"), a broad-accurate code, never a wrong specific cause. Fragile but not misleading. Not a finding (note-only).
- **explain_criterion unknown-kind → command_failed** — honest broad fallback. Accurate.
- **exit codes / reconciler dispositions** — accurate.

### One borderline AMBIGUOUS, deferred (not a new ticket)
- **`config_unreadable` for a malformed-but-readable config** (ConfigError branch): "unreadable" implies an I/O read failure, but the scenario set includes "read fine, failed schema validation." Mildly under-fits. It is a DELIBERATE operator ruling (39f8-ae7c) and low-value, so recording it here rather than filing; revisit only if a broader-accurate name (e.g. `config_invalid`) is wanted.

### Final tallies (post-re-triage)
- MISLEADING (correctable via existing broad-accurate `command_failed`, ready-to-fix): the `llm_unavailable` class at 3 code sites → 5f96, 7d47, fbc0 (+ the pre-existing 73d8/551b, which the same one-line change resolves toward `command_failed`).
- AMBIGUOUS needing a contract decision (escalate): 1 → f75f.
- Vocabulary-registration gap (ready-to-fix): 1 → 0aee.
- Accurate-but-broad, NOT findings: branch-7/NEEDS_INVESTIGATION/missing-extra/deps-sniff/criterion-fallback/exit-codes.
- Borderline deferred: config_unreadable(malformed).

**Prevention recommendation is unchanged and stronger under this bar:** the exhaustive `LLMError` subclass→code contract test should assert each subclass maps to an accurate-fit code (genuine availability types → `llm_unavailable`; all others → `command_failed` or a deliberately-declared finer code), so a new subclass cannot silently inherit the misleading `llm_unavailable`.

comments.body:
## Implementation brief — error-code remediation stack (all decisions RESOLVED)

The audit is complete and every decision is made. This epic is ready to execute as ONE coordinated held-out-TDD Gerrit stack. Authoritative principle and per-child plan:

### Unified principle (the one honest rule)
Reserve **`llm_unavailable`** for genuine availability faults only — `isinstance(exc, LLMUnavailableError)` (incl. `LLMConfigError`): extra absent, credentials missing/invalid, provider unreachable/rate-limited/refused. Route **every other `LLMError` subclass** to the existing broad-but-accurate **`command_failed`** ("an unclassified rebar command failure") — it makes no false cause claim. **Discriminate by exception TYPE, not by phase.** Do NOT invent finer codes (input_rejected on the *error-code* vocabulary, output_invalid, …) unless a consumer demonstrably needs the distinction — grow vocabulary only on observable need (35ab/551b precedent).

### Per-child plan and stack order (bottom → top of the relation chain)
1. **f75f** (core): narrow `error_code_for` branch 6 in `src/rebar/_errors.py` to map only `LLMUnavailableError` → `llm_unavailable`; all other `LLMError` → `command_failed`. This single change also **resolves 7d47** (WorkflowError family) and the 73d8/551b tension (a genuine execute-time outage is an `LLMUnavailableError` and stays `llm_unavailable`; an `ExpressionError` is not → `command_failed`).
2. **fbc0**: `_structured_llm_failure` (the 4 MCP gate tools) — stop hardcoding `error=llm_unavailable`; call `error_code_for(exc)` so the type discrimination applies uniformly.
3. **7d47**: add the observable test proving `render_workflow` MCP tool now surfaces the WorkflowError family as `command_failed`, not `llm_unavailable` (rides f75f; assert through the tool's JSON).
4. **0aee**: register `pinned_ticket_read_failed` in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (vocabulary-contract gap — the code is emitted but unregistered).
5. **5f96** (Option B, operator-approved): split the overloaded `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean in `gate_dispatch.py` — keep it True only for real outages; add a distinct `input_rejected` signal for `LLMInputRejectedError`; update the 3 readers (`plan_review/drift_floor.py:202`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py:468`, `review_bot/adapter.py:114`). Do NOT add a broad `degraded` category (explicitly rejected by the operator).

### Epic-level prevention guardrail (acceptance criterion for the epic)
Add an **exhaustive `exception → code` contract test** over `LLMError.__subclasses__()` (every subclass maps to the intended code, asserted by type), plus a **vocabulary-closure test** (every code any producer can emit ∈ `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` — this pins 0aee and prevents future unregistered codes). These are the regression oracles that make the whole class un-regressable.

### Discipline
Held-out TDD: behavioral tests assert the observable error code **through the real surface** (CLI exit + JSON, MCP tool JSON), RED-for-right-reason first; implementer sees happy-path only. Land as a Gerrit relation-chain stack in the order above; close children bottom-up; each change carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer + DCO. No `--force` anywhere; gates run unbounded.

Else add exactly the missing observable test.

## Problem
A misleading error code is a significant failure mode: it causes LLM/agent consumers to make erroneous assumptions and act on a wrong diagnosis (e.g. "the AI provider is down" when the real fault is bad input or a missing asset). Recent bugs are all instances of ONE systemic pattern: the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` fallthrough in the `error_code_for` classifier mislabels non-availability failures.

## Goal
Systematically audit EVERY error-code / classification surface so each returned code accurately and specifically describes the actual condition, and no failure degrades to a misleading catch-all.

## Reconciled taxonomy (RESOLVED — supersedes the pre-dbca brief)
Epic dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d has since LANDED (closed; commits ae4f6c1a, f854924b) and already reclassified the workflow caller-input family with FINER, more descriptive codes than a broad `command_failed`. Per the operator descriptiveness bar a finer accurate code is strictly better, so dbca's answer is preserved, not competed with. The authoritative target for this epic is therefore:
- `LLMUnavailableError` / `LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable` (genuine availability faults only).
- `LLMRunnerError` subtree (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError`, `ContextWindowExceededError`, `LLMInputRejectedError`, `RunawayToolLoopError`, `StructuredOutputError`/`UnretryableOutputError`/`CompletionRecoveryError`) -> `command_failed` (the residual mislabel this epic fixes).
- dbca workflow caller-input subtree (`WorkflowNotFoundError` -> `not_found`; `WorkflowParseError`/`WorkflowValidationError`/`WorkflowVersionError`/`WorkflowUnknownStepError` -> `invalid_input`) -> PRESERVED UNTOUCHED.
- bare `WorkflowError` base + bare `LLMError` -> `llm_unavailable` (dbca's pinned catch-all; the still-open escalated ticket 551b owns any future change to the bare-base editor/missing-bundle code — this epic does NOT pre-decide it).
Discriminate by exception TYPE, not by phase. Do NOT revert dbca. Do NOT invent new fine-grained error codes beyond what a consumer demonstrably needs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py) routes the `LLMRunnerError` subtree to `command_failed` while keeping `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable`, and leaves dbca's workflow caller-input taxonomy (`not_found`/`invalid_input`) and the bare `WorkflowError`/`LLMError` catch-all (`llm_unavailable`) untouched (child f75f-5509-10c0-4430).
- [ ] `_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py) derives its top-level `error` field via `error_code_for(exc)` instead of hardcoding `llm_unavailable`, across all 4 MCP gate tools, so both dbca's finer codes and the LLMRunnerError routing apply uniformly (child fbc0-ee15-9d69-49ae).
- [ ] The `render_workflow` MCP tool surfaces the `WorkflowError` caller-input family as `not_found`/`invalid_input` (NOT `llm_unavailable`) — already proven observably by the landed dbca contract tests (tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py). 7d47-2131-42bd-4832 is therefore closed as SUPERSEDED by dbca; no `command_failed` is re-asserted for that family.
- [ ] `pinned_ticket_read_failed` is registered in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (child 0aee-a70d-045b-48a1).
- [ ] The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean is True only for genuine `LLMUnavailableError` outages; `LLMInputRejectedError` instead sets a distinct `input_rejected` signal (via a shared `failure.degrade_cause_flags` helper applied in BOTH degrade builders — `gate_dispatch.py` and `plan_review_recovery.py`), and the three readers (`plan_review/drift_floor.py`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `review_bot/adapter.py`) are updated to read it. No broad `degraded` category (child 5f96-25aa-af9d-4f57).
- [ ] A prevention guardrail lands: an exhaustive `exception -> code` contract test over the `LLMError` subclass tree asserting the RECONCILED taxonomy above (availability -> `llm_unavailable`; `LLMRunnerError` subtree -> `command_failed`; dbca workflow subtree -> `not_found`/`invalid_input`; bare bases -> `llm_unavailable`), plus a vocabulary-closure test asserting every code any producer can emit is in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (pins 0aee).
- [ ] [non-codebase] Every change lands via Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`, carries a `rebar-ticket` trailer + DCO sign-off, and children are closed bottom-up.

## Scope (surfaces enumerated by the audit)
- `error_code_for` mapping (`src/rebar/_errors.py`) — the residual blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch 7 (branch 6 workflow classification already handled by dbca).
- `_structured_llm_failure` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) across the 4 MCP gate tools.
- The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean (`gate_dispatch.py` + `plan_review_recovery.py`) and its three readers.
- Top-level `_errors.py` `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary contract.

## Constraints
Remediation lands via Gerrit per AGENTS.md. No --force. Gates run unbounded. dbca (landed) is preserved, not reverted. 551b remains OPEN and owns the bare-`WorkflowError`-base editor/missing-bundle decision — this epic explicitly does not resolve it.
